description:
Did You Know You Are Made of Stardust?

Episode 90 of a daily journey through the universe. ✨
Season 5 finale: where the atoms in your body came from. Hydrogen from the Big Bang, carbon and oxygen made in stars, iron from exploding stars, and gold from colliding neutron stars. Most of your body's mass was made inside stars.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 91: Next stop: Jupiter's biggest night of the year, at opposition February 10 to 11.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

Images: NASA (public domain)
Narration: AI voice

#space #stardust #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: The atoms in your body were made inside stars. Here's how they got to you.
Ninety episodes. We've traveled across the universe. For the finale, let's look at the most amazing place of all: you.
segments.headline: The finale: you

segments.text: The hydrogen in the water in your body was made in the Big Bang, almost fourteen billion years ago.
segments.headline: Hydrogen from the Big Bang

segments.text: But the carbon in your cells, and the oxygen you breathe, were made inside stars, by nuclear fusion.
segments.headline: Carbon and oxygen from stars

segments.text: When big stars die, they explode as supernovas, scattering those elements into space, along with iron, like the iron in your blood.
segments.headline: Scattered by supernovas

segments.text: Remember episode twelve? Gold and other heavy elements were forged when neutron stars collided.
segments.headline: Gold from collisions

segments.text: That star dust drifted through space, collected into clouds, and formed new stars and planets. Including the Sun, and Earth.
segments.headline: New stars from old

segments.text: Most of the mass of your body was made inside stars. You are literally made of stardust.
As Carl Sagan put it, we are a way for the universe to know itself. Thank you for traveling with us.
segments.headline: Thank you

segments.text: The journey continues tomorrow. Jupiter is about to have its biggest night of the year. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for tomorrow's stop.
